title: Service contract for linking biodiversity to national economic and social priorities in the Member States.
description: The contract will provide an analysis of relevant socio-economic priorities and identify synergies between them and biodiversity objectives in EU Member State. It will provide recommendations on how these synergies can be best exploited, with a view to maximise the benefits for economy, society and environment and to optimise the use of public resources by implementing most cost-effective solutions. The contract will evaluate economic and social benefits stemming from these synergies and provide Member State-specific data that will feed into the European Semester process in order to raise the profile of natural capital and its contribution towards Member States' macro-economic policies.

title: Service contract for providing support in relation to the implementation of the Council Directive of 12.12.1991 concerning the protection of waters against pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources (91/676/EEC).
description: The objective of this service contract is to support DG Environment on technical, scientific and socio-economic aspects of nutrients' use and management in the agricultural sector and assist the Commission in its obligation to enforce the Nitrates Directive. In particular, the service contract will address the specific needs linked to:— the provision of scientific, socio-economic and technical advice on an ad hoc basis on issues linked directly or indirectly to the Nitrates Directive,— the production of reports concerning scientific, technical and socio-economic issues related to nutrients' use and management including the Nitrates Directive implementation,— the analysis and commenting of reports submitted to the Commission within the context of a derogation granted in accordance with Annex III.2(b) of the Nitrates Directive,— the production of the necessary background for the Commission to produce detailed and summary reports on implementation of the Nitrates Directive at EU level, based on the reports submitted by Member States.

title: Service contract for further development of EU water balances at sub-catchment level - preparatory action - development of prevention activities to halt desertification in Europe.
description: The objective of this call for tender is to produce revised and complete European water resource balances (quantity, quality) with monthly resolution at sub-basin level. The project should address and mitigate the most relevant data gaps (as well as methodological gaps induced by the absence of data) so that water balances can be established at sub-catchment level for the whole EU with at least the level of confidence achieved in the group of best documented basins to allow better comparability across Europe, at the end of the contract. It should as well validate those components of the water balance that could not be finalised because of these data gaps. The present project should also contribute to the design and prototyping of a permanent and cost-effective process for the production of water balances, improving the interaction between reconstructed and reported data.http://ec.europa.eu/environment/water/index_en.htm

title: Framework contract for information and communication services in the field of the environment (5 lots).
description: External communication in DG Environment is regarded as an integral part of the overall operation — supporting the conception and implementation of policy. Therefore, in close cooperation with technical policy units, the Communication Unit and the Publications Team regularly organise activities aiming to:— build understanding, support and acceptance for our policies,— make DG Environment's activities better known, and raise the Commission's profile as a key player in environmental matters on the international arena,— advocate a resource-efficient society by raising awareness about environmental issues among the general public and encouraging citizens to take positive actions,— encourage stakeholders and opinion leaders to adopt and promote environmentally friendly actions in their field of activity, namely through facilitating the exchange of best practices and by rewarding consistent efforts.The objective of the contract is to ensure that DG Environment has tools to acquire external services necessary to effectively, efficiently and coherently implement its external communication activities. The services covered by the tender are grouped into 5 lots corresponding to given professional sectors:— lot 1 'Event and exhibition organisation, materials and services',— lot 2 'Paper and electronic publication services, app design, writing, graphic design, translations and editorial work',— lot 3 'Evaluation of communication activities and products',— lot 4 'Promotional articles and participants' kits',— lot 5 'Audiovisual production and support for TV, radio and Web productions.

title: Study on EU integrated policy assessment for the freshwater and marine environment, on the economic benefits of EU water policy and on the costs of its non-implementation.
description: This contract concerns (A) the value of clean water as an input for the European economy; and (B) integrated policy assessment in the context of all EU water and marine environment legislation. Part A will serve to increase the understanding of the full value of water and water services and how water resources contribute to economic development and citizens' well-being. It will provide more insight into the functioning of the Water Framework Directive. Part B will support the Commission's policy assessment capacity which is centred around models of the physical, chemical and biological aspects of freshwater and marine environments. These models are held by the Commission and are not part of this contract. Instead, the contract will help in collecting and preparing input data on environmental pressures, costs and performance of measures to be taken, definition of scenarios, and socio-economic assessment of the model output.

title: Service contract for the implementation of Euro 6 light-duty vehicle pollutant emission standards in the EU and benchmark Euro 6 against international emission standards.
description: The European Commission's Directorate-General for Enterprise (DG ENTR) and Directorate-General for the Environment (DG ENV) see the need for a study to inform the debate with stakeholders on the implementation of Euro 6 standards, in particular on the costs and time involved to implement the technologies needed for upcoming Euro 6 emission standards. In order to orient the current debate it is moreover necessary to see Euro 6 standards in an international context and to benchmark them against emission standards in force in other parts of the world. The general purpose of the assignment is to provide support to the Commission in its implementation of the Euro 5/6 legislation. The legislation requires the Commission to propose a Euro 6 emission testing method which reflects emissions under 'normal conditions'. In this aim the Commission wants to bring forward real-world emission testing methodology and reliable statistical evaluation methods not later than 2013. This contract supports this action.

title: Technical assistance for the monitoring of LIFE projects (action grants and operating grants), communication about the LIFE programme and other linked activities.
description: The contractor is required to assist the Commission with the implementation of the LIFE programme during all phases of the project management. This will include, amongst other activities, the monitoring of all open projects (approximately 850 projects) co-financed by the LIFE programme under all LIFE Regulations, support for monitoring of environmental NGOs under the LIFE+ operating grants and communication activities. A single full-time expert should monitor approximately 16–20 projects. For communication activities 12 people are foreseen.All correspondence from the projects should be evaluated using standard model forms prepared by the Commission. This includes progress reports, reports linked to payment requests for additional clauses. Projects must also be visited annually. The contractor should ensure expertise in all 3 parts of the programme. Expertise for LIFE 'Nature' includes notably knowledge of nature conservation management, the 'Birds' and 'Habitat' Directives and nature conservation at local level. Expertise for LIFE 'Environment' includes notably knowledge in the areas of climate change, water, air, soil, urban environment, noise, chemicals, environment and health, waste and natural resources, forest, innovation and strategic approaches. Expertise for LIFE 'Information' includes notably knowledge in the areas as in LIFE 'Nature', LIFE 'Environment' and forest fire prevention. More information about the LIFE programme can be found on the website http://ec.europa.eu/environment/life/index.htm Assistance in communication activities will be requested and expertise is required for the creation and management of publications, multimedia information sources and events. The contract will include the following activities:1. technical and administrative assistance for tasks related to monitoring of the implementation of projects under the LIFE+ action grants;2. support for monitoring of environmental NGOs under the LIFE+ operating grants;3. communication activities: technical and administrative assistance related to communication activities at EU level concerning the LIFE+ programme, their action grants and NGOs' operating grants.Objectives:Ad 1) Action grants:The Commission is seeking technical and administrative assistance for tasks related to implementation of projects under the LIFE+ and LIFE III programmes. The objective of this contract is to assist the Commission in this work. The contractor shall assist the Commission by following and assessing the project's progress at the technical and financial levels and ensure its coherence with the incurred costs. They shall act strictly as an advisory body to the Commission and shall not be involved in the management of the financial resources. The contractor shall be independent from the projects. As an advisory body of the Commission, they shall review the projects and provide technical and financial assessments of the reports submitted to the Commission, as well as providing technical and financial guidance to the projects. The contractor shall not be authorised to take any decision on behalf of the Commission.Ad 2) Operating grants:The broad objective of this contract is to provide independent, external expertise to assist Environment DG in the monitoring of the beneficiaries of NGO grants under LIFE, and the assessment of their individual and collective performance and achievements, through: — detailed review and assessment of financial and technical reports for the beneficiaries,— monitoring visits (audits) to a selection of 8 beneficiaries.The NGO monitoring has the following purposes:— to provide the Commission with information in view of the approval of final reports and calculation of final payments,— to provide the Commission with detailed information on selected beneficiaries' compliance with the provisions of the Grant Agreement, the quality of their financial, managerial and administrative systems as well as the quality of the activities carried...

title: Data Sets on Quality of Drinking Water Supplied – Exceedances, Incidents and Derogations
description: The objective of this contract is to create a technical basis for the new monitoring requirements so that the implementation of the new rules under the revised Drinking Water Directive (DWD) can be tracked at EU level. More precisely, the contract aims to:1) collect examples of best practices and lessons learnt of existing reporting set ups in line with the INSPIRE Directive;2) in close cooperation with the EEA, define a conceptual model for monitoring results, incidents and derogations and consult the Member States on the content for these data sets;3) list options on how national data sets could be managed.

title: European Monitoring of Biodiversity in Agricultural Landscapes (EMBAL) 2028
description:
OBJECTIVES:
The general objectives of this contract are to contribute towards i) the establishment of a robust data series on the state of biodiversity in agricultural landscapes in the EU, and ii) a better understanding of (the impacts of policy actions on) the biodiversity trends in agricultural landscapes at the EU and national level. 
The specific objectives of this contract are i) to undertake the EMBAL field survey in all EU Member States in 2028 and 2029, and ii) to analyse the collected data. The contract will survey at least 4500 sites in each year (i.e. undertake at least 9 000 site-surveys across the two years), strictly following the EMBAL survey protocol and technical guidelines as prepared and executed in the EMBAL survey 2022/2023. 

TASKS:
1) Preparation of the field survey (including sampling strategy and design, pre-processing of monitoring sites, selection and recruitment of surveyors, material and equipment, digitised data workflow, helpdesk, quality control and contingency planning);
2) Execution of the field survey;
3) Data post-processing;
4) Data analysis;
5) Organisation of a conference to present the results. 

KEY DOCUMENTS AND LINKS:

1) EMBAL survey protocol and technical guidelines: 

https://biodiversity.europa.eu/europes-biodiversity/nature-restoration/reference-portal-for-nature-restoration-regulation/documentation/embal-toolkit.7z 

2) EMBAL 2022/2023 dataset: 

https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/723355a8-e549-4691-9c0d-83ab7fc7a0c4

3) EMBAL 2022/2023 analytical report: 

https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/a4444ad4-16b0-11f1-8870-01aa75ed71a1/language-en 

4) EMBAL 2022/2023 appendix to the analytical report: 

https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/8f047e20-16af-11f1-8870-01aa75ed71a1/language-en

title: FRAMEWORK CONTRACT ON TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE AND SCIENTIFIC SUPPORT TO THE NITRATES DIRECTIVE, AGRICULTURE, SOIL AND FOREST POLICIES
description:
Our unit ENV.D1 needs technical assistance and scientific advice on various policies the unit is working on. A Framework contract has been created to cover this need. 
Specifically, our unit has identified a need for technical and scientific advice in the following areas: a) on agricultural related EU policies and initiatives as well as on the environmental dimension of agriculture and the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP.); b) on aspects related to the implementation of the Nitrates Directive and the follow-up of the evaluation of the Nitrates Directive; c) on the implementation of the Soil Monitoring Law (SML); d) on the implementation and follow-up of the EU Forest Strategy and forest related aspects of environmental policy and actions on integrated wildfire risk management. 
Area a) and b) will be covered by Lot 1; Area c) by Lot 2; Area d) by Lot 3

title: Support to stakeholders for implementation & mainstreaming of Environmental Footprint (EF) methods
description:
The objective of this contract is to ensure input from and the participation of environmental NGOS, consumer NGOs and organizations representing SMEs into relevant existing & any future expert groups and any other aspects related to the Environmental Footprint (EF) methods (see below). 

The Environmental Footprint (EF ) Steering Committee and the Technical Advisory Board Expert Groups. The first group includes representatives of the European Commission, Member States, main stakeholder groups (environmental NGOs, consumers and SMEs) and economic sectors. The second group includes environmental footprint and life cycle assessment experts. In these expert groups other EF related aspects such as methodological choices of the EF methods or specific modelling requirements of the datasets are discussed. 
For supporting the potential implementation of the Green Claims Directive, the Commission may create a new expert group. The representation of the SMEs and environmental and consumer NGOs is crucial to ensure that its implementation is balanced and inclusive.

title: SUPPORT TO POLICY DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF LEGISLATION FOR PREVENTION, PREPARATION AND RESPONSE OF MAJOR ACCIDENTS INVOLVING CHEMICAL SUBSTANCES
description:
The purchase aims to provide administrative, scientific and technical support to the Commission and Member States for implementation and development of EU policy associated with the prevention and control of major-accident hazard (Seveso III Directive).
 In particular the project will aim to provide assistance to the Commission in following areas: 
- to promote exchanges and sharing of information, good practices and lessons learnt on implementation of the Seveso-III Directive, with and between Member States. 
- to support the work of the Technical Working Groups on Inspections (TWG2) promoting common approaches to Seveso-III Directive implementation across Member States and consistent inspection and risk management across 11 000 highly diverse industrial sites covered by the Seveso-III Directive. 
- to provide technical assistance for the drafting of technical documentations and guidances supporting harmonised implementation of some provisions of the Seveso-III Directive. 
- to provide expertise, on an ad hoc basis, on some technical issues related to the implementation of the Seveso-III Directive.
- to provide scientific support to the European Commission for risks and accidents analysis and for dissemination of lessons learnt. 
This purchase is necessary to address the implementation issues identified in the MS national reports on implementation of the Seveso III Directive and to take over tasks currently performed by the Major Accidents Hazard Bureau whose activities should be discontnued by the end of the year.

title: Support to the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund
description: The objective of this contract is to support the Commission for the organisation of an Informal global dialogue on Digital Sequence Information and the Cali Fund, to ensure the continuation of the informal process on DSI until COP17, and offer opportunities to build mutual trust and common understanding amongst Parties and stakeholders involved. For this, a workshop would take place in the first semester of 2026, with a view to initiate in-depth discussion on the critical unresolved issues of Decision 16/2, to maintain the momentum on CBD COP16 Decision 16/2, and to promote contribution to the Cali Fund. A second workshop to strengthen the dialogue may be needed in the second half of 2026, with a view to continue discussion on outstanding issues and prepare the ground for negotiations at CBD COP17 in October 2026.

title: Support for the implementation of the EU pledge on three billion additional trees by 2030
description: The EU pledge for three billion additional trees in the EU was announced in 2020 (EU Biodiversity Strategy). The implementation of the pledge depends greatly on initiatives at national and subnational level. A roadmap for its implementation with milestones was published in 2021 (EU Forest Strategy). Building on the accomplished milestones (https://environment.ec.europa.eu/strategy/biodiversity-strategy-2030/3-billion-trees_en), the contractor will further promote the implementation of the EU pledge. In particular, it will promote the uptake of the pledge by liaising with potentially interested stakeholders (public and private organisations of land and forest owners, foresters, national and sub-national authorities) in all Member States; it will organise webinars and seminars/conferences; it will support the Commission on the outreach and organisation of the yearly three billion trees award.

title: Level(s) Maintenance
description: The general objective of the contract is to keep Level(s) up to date in relation to the developing ecosystem in which the assessment framework is situated. Beyond policy development, this includes e.g. evolving standards of both technical and cost nature, as well as LCA software and databases. As Level(s) is developed with the clear objective of being firmly anchored in the current ecosystem, based on existing standards and link to support tools, the framework requires regular updates to continue to maximise its relevance and drive market as well as policy development. The specific objective of the contract is to ensure that Level(s) is firmly linked to EU policy impacting buildings, as well as to ensure that Level(s) is attractive to use and provide technical support at a relevant level.

description: The contract will fill some severe knowledge gaps identified in the impact of 2040 climate targets and thereby be a direct contribution to the Green Deal’s call for increasing synergies between climate and biodiversity actions. Specifically, it will 1) better integrate the impacts of climate change and of natural disturbances impacts (e.g. forest fires) on biodiversity, in models used to design climate, energy and land policies and 2) ensure that the scenarios used in biodiversity impact assessment (e.g. BIOCLIMA) are better aligned with the scenarios of climate impact assessments (e.g. CAPRI). This contract is part of ENV Management Plan 2024

title: Technical support to develop noise action plans guidelines
description: The subject of this call for tenders is “Technical support to develop noise action plans guidelines” under the Environmental Noise Directive 2002/49/EC whilst exploring synergies with the underwater measures to be taken by Member States under the Marine Strategy Framework Directive 2008/56/EC. The primary aim of this service request is to provide a technical guidance document to the Commission to consider supporting the competent authorities on effectively drafting noise action plans, as required in Directive 2002/49/EC and explore possible links with the underwater noise mesures to be taken by the competent authorities under Directive 2008/56/EC. Typically, these authorities include ministries, regional or municipal governments, and road, railway, airport, maritime transport and energy authorities. Therefore, the technical guidance document should be focused and easily reused while ensuring that all essential elements are included.

title: The health and social benefits of nature and biodiversity protection.
description: The study will explore the potential health and social benefits associated with the protection and enhancement of biodiversity in the EU, it will identify opportunities for further developing and increasing these benefits, it will identify possible tools for mapping of social values and health benefits that could be linked to natural environment (green spaces including Natura 2000 areas) and also make recommendations on how actions at the EU level could serve to promote the linkages between biodiversity policy and social policy more effectively. The study will pay particular attention to the health and social benefits associated with the Natura 2000 network. The study will evaluate the existing evidence concerning the linkages between biodiversity, public health, social cohesion and human well-being, identify the stakeholders that are most concerned with the biodiversity/health/social inclusion nexus and related governance issues, identify and present best practice examples. The contract also involves organising a workshop and formulating conclusions and recommendations from the study.

title: Evaluation study to support the fitness check of the Birds and Habitats Directives.
description: The overall aim of the study contract is to assist the European Commission in the preparation of a fitness check of EU nature legislation (Birds and Habitats Directives). This will entail compiling, assessing and synthesising evidence for the fitness check. The study will approach this on the basis of examination of specific questions linked to each of the following categories: relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, and coherence, as well as its EU added value. As a key element of this the study will need to compile evidence and assess: implementation and integration successes and problems; the monetary and non-monetary costs of implementation and of non-implementation of the legislation; the administrative burden of implementation and opportunities for improving implementation without compromising the integrity of the purpose of the Directives; the situation of implementation in different Member States; the views of key stakeholder groups. The mandate for the fitness check is available on the website of the European Commission at http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/legislation/fitness_check/index_en.htm

title: Development of a Population Model and Adaptive Harvest Mechanism for Turtle Dove (Streptopelia Turtur)
description: The European Turtle Dove (Streptopelia turtur) is protected under the Birds Directive (2009/147/EC). Its hunting is allowed under national legislation in ten Member States. When authorising hunting, Member States must ensure that this is compatible with the requirements set out in Articles 2 and 7 of the Directive. A new EU/international Action Plan for the Turtle Dove (http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/wildbirds/hunting/docs/20181002%20Final_draft_European%20TurtleDove.pdf) was approved in May 2018. The action plan identifies the following 3 main threats to the species:1) Habitat loss;2) Illegal killing and trapping;3) Unsustainable hunting levels.The contract aims to set up an adaptive harvest management modelling framework, for each flyway, in accordance with Action 3.2.1 of the Action Plan.

title: Development of tools and services for the water information system for Europe (WISE) and the structured information and implementation framework (SIIF).
description: Due to the integrated approach on water management in the EU, and in order to implement the EU water legislation and, in particular, the Water Framework Directive (WFD) and to achieve the most effective use of the data provided by the Member States' reports, the Commission (DG Environment, the Joint Research Centre and Eurostat), together with the European Environment Agency and the Member States, is developing a water information system for Europe (WISE). The WISE has become a comprehensive and shared European data and information management system for water and is the main reporting tool for water-related legislation. Further development of the WISE system is planned to integrate additional information and to streamline reporting by ensuring information exchange and interoperability at different hierarchical data information levels under all EU water policies and other EU-wide reporting obligations on water.The Commission therefore intends to award a contract for the development of tools and services for WISE in the following areas:1) reporting under EU water policy instruments: focusing on the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC) and the Floods Directive (2007/60/EC) but also including other Directives that are already (to different degrees) integrated in WISE;2) WISE as a shared and distributed system: information exchange and synchronisation of data bases in line with the Inspire Directive, development of the SIIF concept in WISE;3) exploitation and communication of information and its analysis.

title: Establishment of a European Red List of Orthoptera.
description: More than 1 000 species of grasshoppers, crickets and bush-crickets (Orthoptera) occur in Europe. Due to their small distributional ranges, these species are excellent indicators for the identification and conservation of biodiversity hotspots. They are very sensitive to land use changes and therefore often used as bioindicators in environmental impact assessments.A European Red List of Orthoptera is a useful tool to assess the conservation value of sites in environmental impact assessments and to identify gaps in the conservation network. Threatened species will gain more attention, stimulating conservation actions by national authorities. This Red List shall complement the series of Red Lists the Commission has financed so far:http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/species/redlist_en.htm

title: Study on resource efficiency and fiduciary duties of investors.
description: The role of investors as owners of part of the economy brings into question the legal interpretation of 'fiduciary duty', or preservation of the investor's best interest, in particular for asset managers, advisors or trustees. It is sometimes argued that fiduciary duty should encompass not only financial interests but also social and moral obligations, including environmental concerns. In addition, more and more studies show that resource efficiency and the environment are relevant in many cases for the financial returns of portfolio, their vulnerability to risk, and their long term resilience. The question of fiduciary duty has also been identified as a key issue in the Resource Efficiency Finance Roundtable.A study on this topic is, therefore, necessary in order to assess the existing frameworks as well as possible courses of action.This study will study existing provisions on fiduciary duty in various Member States and outside the EU, as well as recent work on materiality and legal implications of integrating sustainability issues in fiduciary duty, and explore desirable options for this integration.

title: Pilot Project: Making the Iron Gates Dams Passable for Danube Sturgeon
description: The objectives of this pilot project is to assess technical solutions for opening a migration route for sturgeon at the Iron Gate hydropower dams on the Danube river on the border between Romania and Serbia. There is no ready-to-use design/solution and considering the size of the dams (among the largest in Europe), the size of the fish (up to 7 meters) and also the local terrain surrounding the Iron Gates, the project necessitates innovative approaches. The project will have clear EU added value as it will contribute to achieving the environmental objectives of the water framework directive, the habitats directive as well as the Bern Convention. It will also promote cross-border co-operation between the EU and its neighbours.

title: Development of a Population Model and Adaptive Harvest Mechanisms for Turtle Dove (Streptopelia turtur)
description: The European Turtle Dove (Streptopelia turtur) is protected under the Birds Directive (2009/147/EC). Its hunting is allowed under national legislation in ten Member States. When authorising hunting, Member States must ensureThat this is compatible with the requirements set out in Articles 2 and 7 of the Directive. A new EU/international Action Plan for the Turtle Dove.(http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/wildbirds/hunting/docs/20181002%20Final_draft_European%20TurtleDove.pdf) was approved in May 2018. The action plan identifies the following three main threats to the species:1) Habitat loss;2) Illegal killing and trapping;3) Unsustainable hunting levels.The contract aims to set up an adaptive harvest management modelling framework, for each flyway, in accordance with Action 3.2.1 of the Action Plan.

title: Development of a method for assessing real world emissions of hybrid diesel light duty vehicles.
description: The European Commission's DG for Enterprise (DG ENTR) and DG for Environment (DG ENV) are seeking support for the implementation of the Euro 5/6 legislation for hybrid diesel cars. They are therefore commissioning a service contract on the technology needed to make Euro 5 and 6 (NEDC) diesel hybrids compliant to Euro 6 RDE standards. This study will equally focus upon the testing and statistical methodology to determine compliance with the Euro 5/6 regulations.The legal requirement for the Commission to present a method which reflects emissions 'under normal driving conditions' accounts for all cars, including hybrid diesels. As expressed in the CARS2020 Communication (1), the Commission wants to bring forward legally binding real-world emission testing methodology and reliable statistical evaluation methods no later than 2017. As of 2014 this methodology will already be used for consumer information, in parallel with the legally binding NEDC based method. The primary objective is to develop an emission testing method based on PEMS, applicable for hybrid diesels.A secondary aim of this assignment is providing data and background information which can be used to widely inform stakeholders and the public on the environmental performance of Euro 5 and Euro 6 (NEDC type approved) Diesel Hybrid technology.(1) Communication from the Commission COM(2012) 636, http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=COM:2012:0636:FIN:EN:PDF

title: Operation of an EU helpdesk for the support and promotion of the eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS).
description: The Unit Sustainable Production and Consumption of the Directorate-General for the Environment aims to ensure the implementation of sustainable policies and voluntary approaches for industry as well as the development and promotion of integration of environmental requirements into industry and the internal market. 1 of the voluntary instruments the Unit has successfully implemented for almost 20 years is the EU eco-management and audit scheme (EMAS). EMAS is a management tool for companies and other organisations to evaluate, report and improve their environmental performance. The scheme has been available for participation by companies since 1995 and was originally restricted to companies in industrial sectors. Since 2001, however, EMAS has been open to all economic sectors including public and private services. Since 2009 EMAS has also developed itself into an environmental instrument that is applicable worldwide.The aim of the EMAS helpdesk services contract will be to perform work to support the implementation and promotion of the EMAS scheme. Currently around 4 500 organisations with over 12 000 sites in Europe and the world use the EMAS instrument to voluntarily improve their environmental performance continuously. Organisations that fulfil all requirements described in the EMAS Regulation (EC No 1221/2009) and use an independent EMAS verifier to verify the correct implementation can become EMAS registered. The EMAS helpdesk services described in this contract are not only instrumental to a correct implementation of the EMAS scheme, but also aim at promoting the scheme to outside the EMAS community with the goal of maintaining and preferably increasing the number of EMAS registrations. The ultimate goal being an increased contribution of the scheme to an improved environmental quality in Europe.

title: Framework contract for services to move towards good environmental status of the European marine waters by implementing the Marine Strategy Framework Directive.
description: The overall objective of this framework contract is to provide services for the Marine Unit in DG Environment in relation with Directive 2008/56/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17.6.2008 establishing a framework for community action in the field of marine environmental policy (Marine Strategy Framework Directive) (MSFD) in order to achieve or maintain ‘Good environmental status’ (GES). Furthermore, it will support the coherence of the implementation of the MSFD within and amongst marine regions and ensure consistency with the legal obligation under EU legislation and international agreements. This process should be implemented in an interactive way, through technical meetings and workshops, consultation with the Member States, the regional sea conventions and the involvement of stakeholders and of the scientific community.

title: Biodiversity protection through results-based remuneration of ecological achievements.
description: The general objective of this call is to provide for the necessary conceptual framework and the operational toolbox that would support the development of result-based agri-environment payment schemes (RBPSs) across the EU. This would entail creating a network of excellence and expertise on these schemes across the EU.The specific objectives are thus the following:1. to provide an up-to-date inventory and review of existing RBPSs in the EU and in EFTA countries;2. to establish a website which presents the existing initiatives in the EU and in EFTA countries;3. to develop a conceptual framework for the description and design of RBPSs which can be applied to different ecosystems and purposes and which enables systematic comparison of existing schemes;4. to produce a 'hands-on' manual detailing the steps to be followed and issues to be covered and addressed when designing and managing an RBPS;5. to organise a 2-day conference to exchange information among those that are currently leading or involved in the development and management or the analysis of RBPSs in the EU and in EFTA countries;6. to establish a European platform for the exchange of experiences and best practices on RBPSs.

title: Regulatory provisions governing key aspects of unconventional gas extraction in selected EU Member States.
description: The objective of this service contract is to identify and assess environment- and health-related regulatory provisions applicable to unconventional gas in 8 selected EU Member States: Bulgaria, Denmark, Germany, Spain, Lithuania, Poland, Romania and United Kingdom. These countries were selected as illustrative cases based on their geographical, cultural and legal diversity and their possible interest in extracting unconventional gas and in particular shale gas resources.In doing so, the purpose of this service contract is twofold:— to help the European Commission illustrate the elements covered under these national legal provisions and to which extent and in which way the coverage is similar or varies across these 8 Member States, and— to help the European Commission identify potential best regulatory practices or limitations in environment- and health-related regulatory provisions applicable to unconventional gas in these 8 Member States.

description:

The contractor will act as the secretariat of the platform, assisting its members in the implementation of the agreed actions. The contractor will provide text (in Word document) for updates on the website on the EU platform on coexistence between people and large carnivores http://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/conservation/species/carnivores/coexistence_platform.htm
 The contractor will organise 1 annual plenary meeting of 1 day of the platform. The contractor will work directly with the members and will assist them with the organisation of the regional workshops and other ad hoc meetings.

title: Service contract for technical support for an EU platform on coexistence between people and large carnivores.
description: The contractor will be required to carry out the following tasks:Task A — support to the work of the platformCompilation of relevant documents and good practices:The contractor will assist the members of the platform to identify and collect examples of good practices of reduction and/or avoidance of conflicts and experiences of situations in which people successfully coexist with large carnivores.Assistance with the communication plan of the platform:The contractor will assist the Commission and the members of the platform to elaborate a draft communication plan for the platform, to be transmitted through the network of the membership on the umbrella stakeholder groups who make up the platform.The contractor will draft and prepare the lay-out for a 4-page flyer containing up-to-date information on the platform, in all official EU languages apart from Maltese and Irish. The flyers will be printed by the European Commission.Task B — the resource centre of the platformThe resource centre of the platform is a Web-based resource centre which does not duplicate other available resources but will provide links to those in addition to storing unique information, or information not elsewhere available digitally (subject to copyright restrictions).The contractor will update and subsequently maintain the website, exclusively using the technologies under which the site is developed (only static HTML pages), on large carnivores developed as part of the nature web pages of DG ENV.Frequently asked questions (FAQ) service:The contractor will maintain a FAQ section on the website for questions concerning best practice and advice on human–large carnivore conflicts.Regular e-mail circular:The contractor will draft a monthly e-mail bulletin to the members of the platform with news on recent developments of the internal work of the platform, and requests for information and input from the members of the platform. Elements from this circular may also be posted on the bi-monthly updates of the website. The issues of the bulletin will be circulated by DG Environment to the members of the platform.Task C — meetingsAnnual meetings:1 annual meeting of 1 day of the platform will serve 2 purposes: 1) stock-taking on the progress made on the thematic tasks and inviting feedback from members; and 2) opportunities for networking between the platform members. The contractor will have to prepare the invitee list, the agenda, meeting documents and provide experts experienced in facilitating discussion on human–large carnivore conflicts, and prepare the minutes.Workshops:The platform will decide on maximum 2 thematic/regional workshops which should be organised in the Member States. The contractor will provide assistance to both the Commission and the members of the platform for these workshops on similar terms as for the annual meeting, i.e. draft agenda, meeting documents and provide experts to facilitate discussions.The Commission will provide the venue for the annual meeting in Brussels. The venues for the workshops will be decided by the members of the platform and the cost of these venues, if any, will be borne by the members of the platform. There are no expenses for travel or catering at these meetings to be covered from this contract.

title: Supporting the Development of a Roadmap for the Reduction of Whole Life Carbon of Buildings
description: A thorough benchmarking exercise is required to understand the current situation (baseline) of whole life carbon of different kinds of buildings, built or renovated with different levels of sustainability ambition, in different parts of the EU, with different building culture, materials and climate. Equally, the potential of different kinds of solutions to reduce whole life carbon needs to be assessed, on project as well as macro level (with a particular focus on embodied carbon and its links to operational carbon). To support the development of a roadmap and national benchmarking, different stages of development will need to be taken into account, for new built as well as for renovation:• low hanging fruit, available to most project without significant extra cost or expertise;• other already existing solutions, ready to be replicated under certain conditions;• actions currently at innovation/demonstration stage;• expected future development.

title: Service contract to support the EU sixth national report to the Convention on Biological Diversity, and follow-up.
description: Technical support to the Commission for tracking progress at the EU level towards the global Aichi Targets and the related EU biodiversity targets to 2020; for the development of the EU's 6th national report on the global Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020, as well as for carrying out stakeholder discussions on its follow-up. The analysis will draw on data, indicators and assessments from a range of sources including the European Environment Agency, the Joint Research Centre, DG Research and Innovation and Eurostat, and other sources as appropriate. The contractor will assist the Commission in planning and carrying out, as well as in compiling and analysing the results of, stakeholder consultations on implementation and on the post-2020 global agenda. Data and analysis developed in the context of this contract may also feed into further reporting by the Commission. Appropriate links will be ensured with potentially relevant reporting processes.

description:
To provide services to the Water Unit in DG Environment in relation to the following:
— independent, impartial and punctual necessary work and advice on scientific, socio-economic and technical issues related to the issues dealt with within the common implementation strategy (CIS) of the Water Framework Directive (WFD) and Floods Directive (FD),
— technical assistance to the Commission in the integrated assessment of the implementation of the EU water legislation (WFD, Priority Substances Directive, Groundwater Directive and Floods Directive) and 2nd RBMPs/1st FRMPs, looking at issues such as coordination performed by Member States in the different steps in the WFD and the FD planning process and the implementation of other related environmental Directives,
— technical assistance to the Commission in in-depth focused assessments of the WFD/FD implementation in MS on selected issues linked to specific needs,
— technical assistance to assess information on possible infringement cases.

title: Study to support the REFIT evaluation of Directive 2001/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27.6.2001 on the assessment of the effects of certain plans and programmes on the environment (SEA Directive).
description: The overall purpose of this contract is to assist the European Commission in the REFIT evaluation of the Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Directive. The tenderer will have to compile, assess and synthesise evidence for performing the evaluation. The study will address the evaluation on the basis of examination of the following categories: effectiveness, efficiency, relevance and coherence, as well as its EU added value. As a key element of this study the successful tenderer will need to compile evidence and assess: (i) the application of the entire SEA Directive in all EU Member States, including its relation with international treaties; (ii) the situation of implementation in different Member States; (iii) to what extent the SEA Directive has contributed to the environmental concerns to be integrated in the planning, making and adoption process.

title: Support to the implementation of the EU Timber Regulation.
description: The European Union's policy to fight illegal logging and associated trade was defined back in 2003 with the forest law enforcement governance and trade (FLEGT) action plan. It proposed a package of measures to support international effort to tackle the problem. In implementing the action plan the EU has been negotiating voluntary partnership agreements (VPAs) with timber-producing countries (partner countries), which put a legally binding obligation on the parties to implement a licensing scheme and to regulate trade in timber and timber products identified in the agreements.Given the major scale and urgency of the problem, it was necessary to complement and reinforce the FLEGT action plan with additional measures and for that reason Regulation (EU) No 995/2010 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20.10.2010 laying down the obligations of operators who place timber and timber products on the market (the EU Timber Regulation; the EUTR) was adopted and entered into force on 2.12.2010:http://ec.europa.eu/environment/forests/timber_regulation.htmThe Regulation covers a wide range of timber products listed in its annex using EU customs' code nomenclature. It became applicable from 3.3.2013 to allow time for EU operators, timber producers and Member States, as well as trading partners, to be prepared. By June 2012 the Commission adopted necessary non-legislative acts: the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 363/2012, and the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 607/2012. In 2013 the Commission elaborated, in close collaboration with the Member States, a guidance document on the EUTR, where specific aspects of the Regulation were clarified.Although the Regulations are directly binding throughout the EU, Member States are required to take certain specific measures and are responsible for their day-to-day implementation and enforcement.The purpose of the contract is to:1. provide support to the European Commission in assessing applications for monitoring organisations;2. provide support to the European Commission in monitoring the implementation and enforcement of the EUTR, as detailed above;3. provide input to the European Commission, in relation to point 1 and 2 above, for use in the review of the Regulation scheduled for 2015.

title: Phase 2 of the European business and biodiversity platform.
description: Phase 2 of the EU business and biodiversity (B@B) platform is a continuation of the previous platform.The European business and biodiversity (B@B) platform lasted for 3 years and the contract (with IUCN) ended in October. It covered 6 sectors: agriculture, forestry, finance, food supply, non-energy extractive industry and tourism. All the material from workshops, publications, case studies, etc. can be found on http://ec.europa.eu/environment/biodiversity/business/index_en.htmlThe platform was effective in terms of communication activities and increasing awareness of the ways that business can support biodiversity. Some useful best practices related to benchmarking concerning, in particular, the monitoring of biodiversity were also developed.Phase 2 of the EU business and biodiversity (B@B) platform will be open to all business sectors. It will continue some activities of the previous platform and also steer the platform in new directions such as thematic tasks on natural capital accounting, biodiversity and innovation and innovative financing mechanisms for biodiversity in the private sector. The objectives include:1) providing an EU-level forum for a sustained and strategic dialogue concerning the delivery of objectives under the biodiversity strategy to 2020;2) working with business to develop tools and approaches that will promote the integration of biodiversity considerations into business practice;3) supporting the actions being undertaken by Member States by encouraging and promoting potential synergies between different national actions and between the EU level and the national level;4) promoting better communication, increased awareness and improved coordination in relation to business and biodiversity activities.

description: Species status assessment is one of the key avenues to evaluate the success of conservation actions and related policies. One of the available tools for such assessment is the International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List, a highly authoritative and objective methodology for classifying species by their extinction risk. A number of taxonomic groups has been covered by this assessment so far, but not moths — an important group of pollinators. This contract will produce a European Red List of moths.

title: Assessment of Taxonomic Expertise in Europe – ‘European Red List’ of Taxonomists
description: Taxonomic expertise is indispensable for collecting data, information and knowledge on insects, which is in turn necessary to develop and implement effective actions for their conservation. This contract will assess the current state of taxonomic expertise on insects and provide recommendations on how to address the gaps. It will also produce a communication tool — ‘European Red List’ of Taxonomists — in order to raise awareness about the importance of taxonomists, and the problem of their declining numbers.
